**35 Personal allowance**

(1) Subject to subsections (2) to (4), an individual is entitled to a personal allowance of £12,570.

(2) For an individual whose adjusted net income exceeds £100,000 (“the income limit”), the allowance under subsection (1) is reduced by one-half of the excess.

(3) Subsection (2) does not reduce the allowance below nil.

(4) If the amount of the allowance that remains after the operation of subsections (2) and (3) would otherwise not be a multiple of £1, it is to be rounded up to the nearest amount which is a multiple of £1.

(5) For the meaning of “adjusted net income” see section 58.

**6 The basic rate, higher rate and additional rate**

(1) The main rates at which income tax is charged are the basic rate, the higher rate and the additional rate.

(2) For the tax year 2026-27 the basic rate is 20%, the higher rate is 40% and the additional rate is 45%.

**10 Income charged at the basic, higher and additional rates: individuals**

(1) Income tax is charged on an individual's taxable income—

(a) at the basic rate, on so much of it as does not exceed the basic rate limit,

(b) at the higher rate, on so much of it as exceeds the basic rate limit but does not exceed the higher rate limit, and

(c) at the additional rate, on so much of it as exceeds the higher rate limit.

(2) The basic rate limit is £37,700.

(3) The higher rate limit is £125,140.

(4) In this section “taxable income” means the income remaining after allowances are deducted at Step 3 of the calculation in section 23.
